params.desc: Number of solver stages (required).

params.name: ring
params.desc: Case-generation ring: ``'coda'`` (single shared mesh, default), ``'coda_single'`` (one mesh per case via ``mesh_paths``) or ``'horses3d'`` (HORSES3D, one mesh and a ``p`` ladder; it ignores ``eq_type`` and ``num_stages``). Keyword-only; historical positional calls are unaffected.

params.name: **kwargs
params.desc: Forwarded to the ring (see :class:`BaseRing`).

params.name: All other attributes and methods are served by the ring itself
which is only available as ``BaseRing.Backpack`` and is deliberately
Attribute writes (except ``_ring`` itself) are forwarded to the
ring, so the facade and the ring never diverge.

text_sections.title: Examples
text_sections.text:
::

    from FotR import GANDALF

    gdf = GANDALF('/data/TIFON/rans5', eq_type='rans', num_stages=2,
                  version='flowsimulator2024', ring='coda')

Because everything is forwarded, which class a call lands on depends
on the ``ring`` chosen above, and the two rings take different
arguments. Ask the object rather than scrolling back::

    gdf.some_light('generate_folders')   # which ring, and its signature

``Backpack`` is the one name that is never forwarded, so looking it
up on the facade fails; the search finds where it really lives::

    GANDALF.some_light('isa_atmosphere')  # BaseRing.Backpack.isa_atmosphere

doc.summary: Delegate everything (except dunders and Backpack) to the ring.
doc.description:
The facade owns almost nothing: ``define_cases``,
``define_geom_file``, ``add_param``, ``compute_param``,
``generate_folders``, ``assign_jobs``, ``submit_cases``,
``recover_pending_jobs`` and every data attribute
(``df_cases``, ``case_tensor``, ``array_ptos``, ``root_dir``, …)
are served by the ring, so a GANDALF behaves like the ring it
wraps.

params.name: name
params.desc: Attribute being looked up.

returns.desc: The attribute taken from the active ring.

raises.desc: If *name* is a dunder, if it is listed in ``_NON_DELEGATED``, if there is no active ring, or if the ring itself does not have it.

text_sections.title: Notes
text_sections.text:
``_NON_DELEGATED`` currently holds exactly one name,
``'Backpack'``, so ``gdf.Backpack`` raises ``AttributeError``
by design — reach it as ``BaseRing.Backpack`` instead. Note
that ``GANDALF.Backpack`` (on the **class**) fails for a
different reason: ``__getattr__`` only runs for instances, so
that lookup never reaches this method and Python reports
``type object 'GANDALF' has no attribute 'Backpack'``.

doc.summary: Run ``sbatch`` on every case folder, in case order.
doc.description:
Each job is submitted from inside its own case directory, so
relative paths in the shell script resolve as the solver
expects. A case whose script is missing is logged and skipped
rather than aborting the batch.

raises.desc: If ``generate_folders`` has not run (no folders), if ``assign_jobs`` has not run (no ``file_sh`` selected), or if ``sbatch`` is not on PATH — i.e. you are not on a Slurm cluster.

text_sections.title: Notes
text_sections.text:
This actually launches the campaign. ``assign_jobs(submit=True)``
only writes the node and CPU count into each script; nothing
reaches the queue until this call.

methods.name: recover_pending_jobs
methods.signature: recover_pending_jobs(broken_node: str, replacement_node: str, file_sh: Optional[str] = None, dry_run: bool = True)

doc.summary: Reassign pending Slurm jobs that are constrained to a failed node.
doc.description:
The cases are identified using the metadata stored in
``<root_dir>/metadata/cases_metadata.json`` and the working directory
reported by Slurm for each pending job.

The method:
    1. Reads the simulation metadata.
    2. Searches the user's PENDING Slurm jobs.
    3. Identifies jobs requesting ``broken_node``.
    4. Associates each job with its simulation directory.
    5. Shows the proposed changes if ``dry_run=True``.
    6. Otherwise cancels the old job, modifies its ``run.sh`` and
    resubmits it with ``sbatch``.

params.name: broken_node
params.desc: Node that is unavailable, e.g. ``"n003"``.

params.name: replacement_node
params.desc: Node to which the affected simulations will be reassigned, e.g. ``"n005"``.

params.name: file_sh
params.desc: Name of the Slurm submission script inside each simulation folder. Defaults to the ``file_sh`` given to :meth:`assign_jobs`, falling back to ``"run.sh"``.

params.name: dry_run
params.desc: If True, only display the proposed operations. If False, actually cancel, modify and resubmit the jobs.

doc.summary: Standalone helpers for building a case campaign.
doc.description:
Atmosphere and fluid properties (:meth:`isa_atmosphere`,
:meth:`Sutherland_law`), geometry conditioning
(:meth:`normalize_airfoil`), Slurm inspection
(:meth:`squeue_terminal`, :meth:`sinfocpu_terminal`) and the
sampling warp used by :meth:`BaseRing.define_cases`
(``_warp_variable``). Everything is a ``@staticmethod``: the
Backpack is never instantiated and holds no state.

text_sections.title: Notes
text_sections.text:
**This is reachable as ``BaseRing.Backpack``, never as
``GANDALF.Backpack``.** The GANDALF facade forwards attribute
lookups to its ring, but ``'Backpack'`` is listed in
``GANDALF._NON_DELEGATED`` and is deliberately excluded, so both
``GANDALF.Backpack`` (on the class) and ``gdf.Backpack`` (on an
instance) raise ``AttributeError``. Import the ring instead::

    from FotR.characters.rings import BaseRing
    T, P, rho = BaseRing.Backpack.isa_atmosphere(h=11000)

``BaseRing`` is not re-exported by ``FotR``, so
``from FotR import BaseRing`` does not work either. A concrete
ring also inherits it (``CODARing.Backpack`` is the same object).

text_sections.title: Examples
text_sections.text:
::

    from FotR.characters.rings import BaseRing

    T, P, rho = BaseRing.Backpack.isa_atmosphere(h=11000)
    mu = BaseRing.Backpack.Sutherland_law(
        mu0=1.716e-5, T=T, Treference=255.55,
    )

Normalise an Nx2 airfoil to chord 1, leading edge at x = 0.

returns.desc: Same type as the input, scaled by the chord.

raises.desc: If *coords* is not two-dimensional with two columns.

text_sections.title: Warnings
text_sections.text:
**The input is modified in place when it is already a float
array.** ``np.asarray`` only copies when it has to change
the dtype, so passing a ``float64`` array leaves the
caller's array shifted and scaled; passing an integer array
happens to copy. Pass ``coords.copy()`` if you need to keep
the original.

doc.description:
Cases come from :meth:`define_cases` (and :meth:`add_param` /
:meth:`compute_param`) as in every ring; :meth:`generate_folders`
writes them, :meth:`submit_cases` launches them through
``utils_H3d/run.sh`` and :meth:`fsp_report` checks the free-stream
preservation tests.

params.desc: Campaign root (``metadata/`` and ``outputs/``).

params.name: eq_type, num_stages
params.desc: Accepted for the GANDALF facade and ignored: the flow equations come from the control template, and the stages of a HORSES3D case are its polynomial orders (``p_levels``).

methods.name: generate_folders
methods.signature: generate_folders(control_template: str, mesh_path: str, tag: str, folder_fmt: str, p_levels: Union[list, tuple] = (2,), control_values: Optional[dict] = None, p_values: Optional[dict] = None, extra_dirs: Optional[list] = None, data_to_update: Optional[dict] = None, setup_dir: Optional[str] = None, run_script: Optional[str] = None, fsp: bool = True, fsp_steps: int = 200, strip_comments: bool = True, overwrite: bool = False)

doc.summary: Write one folder per case under ``outputs/`` and the metadata.
doc.description:
Per case: ``MESH/`` (copy), ``RESULTS/``, ``LOG/``, one ``file_control_p

.control`` per entry of ``p_levels``, the FSP controls (``fsp=True``), ``extra_dirs``, ``SETUP/`` and a ``run.sh`` link. Existing folders are skipped (``exist = True``) unless ``overwrite``. Every control starts from ``control_template`` and is changed key by key, in this order: ``control_values``, the restart ladder, ``p_values[p]``, and the keys the ring owns (``mesh file name``, ``Polynomial order``, ``solution file name``).

params.name: control_template
params.desc: A working ``.control``. Its ``#define`` blocks (boundaries, monitors…) are copied untouched. It must declare every boundary of the mesh; the inner zones (``BCType`` 100, e.g. refinement surfaces) may be left out: HORSES3D still wants a ``type`` for them, so the ring adds a ``#define boundary`` block with ``type = FreeSlipWall`` and says so. That type is never applied: faces with an element on each side stay interior (``Number of faces: 0`` for those zones in the solver log).

params.name: mesh_path
params.desc: HOPR/PyHOPE ``.h5`` mesh. Its name must carry ``g<Ngeo>``.

params.name: tag
params.desc:
Short campaign label for the solution names (``RESULTS/_gp

.hsol``). Letters, digits, ``-`` and ``_``; it must not end in ``_`` (autosave pattern).

params.name: folder_fmt
params.desc: Case folder name, formatted with the design variables, e.g. ``'tsr_{tsr:.1f}_M_{M:.4f}'``.

params.name: p_levels
params.desc: Polynomial orders, ascending, each ``>= g``. The first starts from scratch; each next one restarts from the previous solution (``restart polorder`` = previous ``p``).

params.name: control_values
params.desc: ``{control key: df_cases column or value}`` for every ``p``, e.g. ``{'mach number': 'M', 'final time': 20.0}``. A string naming a column takes the case's value; ``None`` removes the key.

params.name: p_values
params.desc: ``{p: {control key: value}}`` for one level, e.g. a later absolute ``final time`` for ``p=3``. Overrides the ladder.

params.name: extra_dirs
params.desc: Folders copied into each case (e.g. ``ActuatorDef``). Text files in them get ``data_to_update`` substituted.

params.name: data_to_update
params.desc: ``{PLACEHOLDER: df_cases column or literal}``, as in the CODA ring, for the files of ``extra_dirs``.

params.name: setup_dir
params.desc: ``SETUP`` folder (``ProblemFile.f90``, ``Makefile``) copied as ``SETUP/``. Compile it afterwards with ``build_setup.sh``.

params.name: run_script
params.desc: Launcher linked as ``run.sh`` (``utils_H3d/run.sh``). Needed by :meth:`submit_cases`.

params.name: fsp
params.desc:
Also write ``fsp_p

.control`` (see :meth:`fsp_control`). Default True.

params.name: fsp_steps
params.desc: Time steps of the FSP test. Default 200.

params.name: strip_comments
params.desc: Remove ``!`` comments from the controls. Default True.

params.name: overwrite
params.desc: Rewrite the controls, mesh, ``extra_dirs``, ``SETUP`` and ``run.sh`` of existing case folders. ``RESULTS/`` and ``LOG/`` are never deleted. Default False (existing folders are skipped).

raises.desc: Bad ``tag``, ``p_levels`` not ascending or below ``g``, a mesh name without ``g<Ngeo>``, a ring-owned key in ``control_values`` or ``p_values``, a control that would miss a key HORSES3D requires, or a mesh zone without a ``#define boundary`` block (all checked before writing anything).
Missing template, mesh, extra folder, SETUP or run script.

methods.signature: fsp_control(control_text: str, p: int, zones: list, steps: int = 200)

doc.summary: Free-stream preservation test derived from a case control.
doc.description:
The same flow, the same mesh and order, but ``Inflow`` on every
boundary of the mesh and nothing else: no restart, actuator line or
disk, IBM, monitors, probes or saved surfaces. The uniform initial
state is then an exact solution, and a valid mesh (consistent
metric terms, no inverted elements) keeps it to round-off (judge
it with :meth:`fsp_report`). It checks the mesh, not any
physics.

params.name: control_text
params.desc:
The ``file_control_p

.control`` of the case.

params.name: p
params.desc: Polynomial order.

params.name: zones
params.desc: Every zone name of the mesh (``BCNames``). HORSES3D wants a ``type`` for each, inner surfaces included; those have no boundary faces, so ``Inflow`` there changes nothing.

params.name: steps
params.desc: Time steps. Default 200.

doc.summary: Every mesh zone needs a ``#define boundary`` block (HORSES3D stops with "Missing boundary condition type" otherwise); by now the inner ones were added by the ring, so a missing zone is a real boundary.

methods.name: submit_cases
methods.signature: submit_cases(p: Union[int, list, tuple], repo: str, arch: str = 'GPU', node: str = 'n001', ngpu: Union[int, dict] = 1, cpus_per_gpu: int = 16, ncpus: Union[int, dict] = 48, branch: Optional[str] = None, solver: str = 'ns', fsp: bool = False, cases: Optional[list] = None, dry_run: bool = True)

doc.summary: Launch the control of order ``p`` of every case through ``run.sh``.
doc.description:
Runs ``HORSES3D_REPO=<repo> SOLVER=<solver> ./run.sh <control>
<branch> GPU <node> <ngpu> <cpus_per_gpu>`` (or ``… CPU <node>
<ncpus>``) inside each case folder; ``run.sh`` checks the control,
the solver and ``SETUP`` before calling ``sbatch``. A case whose
solution already has a ``.hsol`` or a ``.residuals`` is skipped.

``p`` may be a list of ascending orders, e.g. ``[2, 3, 4, 5]``: the
restart ladder is then chained. In each case, every order is
submitted with ``DEPENDENCY=afterok:<job of the previous order>``,
so Slurm starts it only when the previous one ends well and cancels
it if that one fails (``run.sh`` adds ``--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes``).
An order already started (skipped) leaves no job to wait for: the
next one is submitted without a dependency and ``run.sh`` then needs
its restart file. If an order fails or has no control, the rest of
that case's chain is not submitted.

The solver repository is always explicit: ``HORSES3D_REPO`` is set
from ``repo`` for every case and any value already in the
environment is ignored. Before planning anything, the repository
must have ``Solver/bin/horses3d.<solver>`` and be on ``branch``.
``SETUP`` must be compiled against the same repository
(``HORSES3D_REPO=<repo> build_setup.sh``); ``run.sh`` checks it.

params.name: p
params.desc: Polynomial order to launch, or ascending orders to chain.

params.name: repo
params.desc: Solver repository (``~`` is expanded), e.g. ``'~/repos/horses3d-gpu'`` or a clone of a development branch such as ``'~/repos/horses3d-gpu-ad'``.

params.name: ngpu
params.desc: GPUs of a GPU run. Default 1. A dict ``{p: n}`` sets them per order, e.g. ``{2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 4}``; it must have every order of ``p``.

params.name: cpus_per_gpu
params.desc: CPUs of each MPI task of a GPU run. Default 16.

params.name: ncpus
params.desc: MPI tasks of a CPU run. Default 48. A dict ``{p: n}`` sets them per order, like ``ngpu``.

params.name: branch
params.desc: Branch ``repo`` must be on. Default: the branch it is on. Never checked out, only compared.

params.name: solver
params.desc: ``ns``, ``ins``, ``mu`` or ``nssa``. Default ``'ns'``.

params.name: fsp
params.desc:
Launch ``fsp_p

.control`` instead (a single order only). Default False.

params.name: cases
params.desc: Folder names. Default: every case.

params.name: dry_run
params.desc: Only report the commands. Default True.

returns.desc: One row per case and order: ``folder``, ``p``, ``control``, ``status`` (``'planned'``, ``'submitted'``, ``'skipped'``, ``'failed'``), ``command``, ``job_id``, ``depends_on`` (job it waits for; ``'<p2>'`` in a dry run) and ``message``.

text_sections.title: Examples
text_sections.text:
::

    repo = '~/repos/horses3d-gpu'
    plan = gdf.submit_cases(2, repo, fsp=True)          # what would run
    gdf.submit_cases(2, repo, fsp=True, dry_run=False)  # from nibbler
    gdf.submit_cases([2, 3, 4, 5], repo, ngpu={2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 4},
                     dry_run=False)                       # chained

doc.summary: Resolve and check the solver repository of :meth:`submit_cases`.
doc.description:
Returns the absolute path of ``repo`` and the branch to pass to
``run.sh``. Raises if the repository or ``Solver/bin/horses3d.<solver>``
is missing, if it is not on a branch (detached ``HEAD``) or if it is
not on ``branch``.

doc.summary: Read the FSP tests of order ``p``: does each mesh keep free stream?
doc.description:
The verdict comes from the solution, not from the residuals: the
final ``.hsol`` is compared node by node with the uniform state the
solver wrote at iteration 0 (``<stem>_0000000000.hsol``). The
residuals are reported for information only: at low Mach they are
far from zero even for an exact uniform state (round-off of large
energy fluxes summed over every degree of freedom: up to 1.6e-4 on
the NTNU turbine mesh, whose solution moved by 5e-9 relative).

params.name: p
params.desc: Polynomial order of the test.

params.name: tol
params.desc: Largest relative change of the solution accepted as round-off. Default 1e-6 (a sound mesh gives ~1e-9 after 200 steps; an inverted or badly stitched element gives orders of magnitude more).

returns.desc: One row per case: ``folder``, ``status`` (``'pending'``, ``'running'`` while the final ``.hsol`` is missing or incomplete, ``'done'``), ``iterations``, ``max_residual``, ``last_residual``, ``max_deviation`` (largest change of any variable, relative to its free-stream scale: density, momentum magnitude, energy), ``worst_element`` (0-based) and ``preserved`` (``max_deviation < tol``).

doc.summary: ``(max relative change, worst element)`` between the iteration-0 and the final solution of an FSP test, or None if either is missing or the final one is incomplete.
